articles.headline: UN COP31 climate talks in Turkey end without major deal
articles.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
articles.summary: United Nations climate negotiations concluded in Antalya, Turkey, without a major new agreement after deep divisions arose over fossil fuels and climate finance. The talks became the longest in history but collapsed because the draft omitted direct references to phasing out fossil fuels and lacked concrete funding commitments for poorer nations. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed deep disappointment over the deadlock.
articles.description: The prime minister of Australia, which co-hosted COP31, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

articles.headline: Democrats secure historic House majority with at least 258 seats
articles.title: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats, largest since 1992
articles.summary: House Democrats won at least 258 seats following a November 22, 2026 sweep, creating a divided government with a Republican White House and a Democratic Senate. Winning 44 additional seats, the party plans a 100-day agenda focusing on cost-of-living issues and oversight investigations. The outcome provides leadership under potential Speaker Hakeem Jeffries with a wide margin while reducing Republicans to 173 seats.
articles.description: Republicans will have at least 173 seats in the minority

articles.headline: Democrats win U.S. Congress control in midterm elections
articles.title: Democrats win U.S. Congress in midterm rout of U.S. President Donald Trump
articles.summary: Democratic candidates secured majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate during the midterm elections held on November 3, 2026. According to projections, the sweeping legislative gains hand the party power to block President Donald Trump's agenda, thwart judicial nominations, and investigate his administration. The wave of upsets included historic victories in reliably Republican strongholds such as Kansas, Iowa, and Texas.
articles.description: The Opposition party also retained key Senate seats, while victory in Georgia’s Governor race added to mounting signs that Republicans face a difficult night

articles.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse in Antalya over fossil fuel phase-out standoff
articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.summary: United Nations climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye, concluded without consensus on November 22, 2026, after a record 48-hour overtime due to disagreements over fossil fuel language. The European Union, backed by roughly 130 nations, rejected the cover text for lacking phase-out commitments. Conversely, nations like India and Saudi Arabia supported the text, stressing the need for equitable energy transitions.
articles.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit collapses in Turkey after nations reject fossil fuel pact
articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.summary: United Nations climate talks in Antalya concluded without agreement on November 22, 2026, after the European Union and several island nations blocked a draft text that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels. Australia led negotiations for a cover decision, but fierce opposition from countries including Ireland and the Marshall Islands resulted in a historic failure during the longest conference in UN history.
articles.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

articles.headline: UN climate talks collapse without a deal
articles.title: UN climate talks collapse without a deal
articles.description: The longest UN climate summit in history ended without a deal in Turkiye, the first such failure since 2009.

articles.headline: Bahrain accuses Iran of industrial site strike as tankers are hit in Hormuz
articles.title: Iran strike wounds two in Bahrain, Riyadh denounces ‘criminal’ attacks
articles.summary: Bahrain accused Iran of targeting a civilian industrial facility on Sitra Island, causing a fire but no casualties, while two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident occurred amid an ongoing maritime conflict and US counterblockade efforts. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated a Qatari delegation visited Tehran for talks, as Tehran maintained its demands for lifting blockades.
articles.description: Bahrain said two people were wounded in an attack on “a civilian industrial site”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted U.S. air defence systems.

articles.headline: Climate talks end without deal after failing to secure consensus
articles.title: ‘Disappointing’: Delegates react after COP31 climate talks end without deal
articles.summary: United Nations climate talks concluded without an overarching agreement after negotiating blocs rejected a draft text presented by Turkiye and Australia. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed profound frustration over the outcome, citing opposition from oil- and gas-producing countries regarding fossil fuel references and adaptation finance targets.
articles.description: Draft text considered too weak to deal with climate change after oil-producing countries oppose the term 'fossil fuels'.

articles.headline: European Union rejects climate deal over lack of fossil fuel mention
articles.title: EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt
articles.summary: The European Union on November 22, 2026, rejected a draft climate agreement at the COP31 summit in Türkiye because it failed to explicitly mention fossil fuels. Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien stated the bloc would not endorse a pact that ignores the primary driver of climate change as negotiations extended into record extra time.
articles.description: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time

articles.headline: India and European Union expected to sign free trade agreement
articles.title: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16
articles.summary: India and the 27-nation European Union are likely to sign a major free trade agreement on December 16 during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Brussels. The deal, which follows two decades of negotiations, aims to provide duty-free access for 93 percent of Indian shipments and create a massive market for two billion people.
articles.description: European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during PM Modi's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force in 2027

articles.headline: Prime Minister Andy Burnham defends landmark EU agreement in Parliament
articles.title: Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'
articles.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will tell Parliament on Monday that a new agreement with the European Union provides a realistic opportunity to improve the British economy over the next decade. The deal addresses food exports and emissions trading, though opposition leaders including Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch and Reform UK leader Nigel Farage sharply criticized the terms and economic projections.
articles.description: The prime minister will tell MPs the deal agreed on Friday is a "choice between a broken status quo or change".

articles.title: Deadly attack in Kyiv as Russia launches barrage against Ukraine

articles.headline: Divya Deshmukh wins women's Chess World Cup in Batumi
articles.title: Teenager Divya outlasts Humpy, emerges India’s first women’s World Cup winner
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old Divya Deshmukh won the women's Chess World Cup in Batumi, Georgia, by defeating fellow Indian player Koneru Humpy in a tiebreaker on November 23, 2026. Alongside the title organised by the International Chess Federation, the victory earned the teenager her Grandmaster title, making her the fourth Indian woman to achieve the distinction.

articles.headline: Russian strikes kill at least 15 people in Kyiv
articles.title: Ukraine says Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region
articles.summary: Russian aerial barrages across the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people on November 23, 2026, as rescue workers searched through the rubble of a partially collapsed residential building in Dymer. Regional officials reported that strikes also hit a supermarket in Vyshneve and a private home in Bila Tserkva, while Moscow continued targeting energy infrastructure ahead of winter.
articles.description: Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year

articles.headline: Indonesian factory fire kills 24 people in Banten
articles.title: Indonesia says 24 killed in factory blaze as rescuers search for dozens missing
articles.summary: Indonesian authorities confirmed that 24 people died in a fire that broke out on November 21, 2026, at a confectionery factory in Cikande, Banten province. Rescuers continued searching through unstable structures for approximately 30 missing workers on November 23. Officials stated that preliminary investigations indicate the blaze may have been caused by an air-conditioner short circuit.
articles.description: Authorities ⁠were still investigating the cause of the fire, which broke out on Saturday (November 21, 2026) evening, in one building of the ‌PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Cikande in Banten province, about an hour’s drive ‌from the capital Jakarta

articles.headline: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Alexander Zverev to win ATP Finals
articles.title: Alcaraz storms past world number one Zverev to win maiden ATP Finals title
articles.summary: Spanish tennis player Carlos Alcaraz defeated world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 in the final to capture his first ATP Finals title. The 23-year-old saved three set points in the tiebreak on Sunday to secure his 14th consecutive victory and complete a dominant end to the season following previous tournament wins in Vienna and Paris.
articles.description: Alcaraz joins an exclusive list, becoming one of only four men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.

articles.headline: India and China hold second round of military talks in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: Why the second round of Corps Commander-level dialogue in Arunachal Pradesh matters
articles.summary: India and China held nearly ten days of Corps Commander-level discussions in Arunachal Pradesh beginning on November 8, 2026, aimed at preventing border tensions along the Line of Actual Control. Lieutenant General Girish Kalia led the Indian delegation alongside a Ministry of External Affairs official during the talks, which focused on addressing competing territorial claims and ongoing military challenges in the Eastern Sector.
articles.description: The second round is aimed at establishing clearer engagement protocols between the two armies, preventing face-offs between patrol parties from escalating into larger confrontations and ensuring that communication channels remain open

articles.headline: US congressional panel urges dialogue with India on Dalai Lama succession
articles.title: U.S. panel urges India dialogue for Dalai Lama succession, warns of China legitimacy contest
articles.summary: A bipartisan United States congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level diplomatic and intelligence channel with India to plan for the 14th Dalai Lama's succession. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission warned that China might turn the reincarnation process into an international legitimacy contest, while urging the recognition of the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole authority.
articles.description: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

articles.title: Trump says he wants ‘permanent’ deal to stop Iran getting nuclear weapons

articles.title: Tata Steel approves sale of tubes & pipes business, Tata Steel Colors to Apollo Tubes for ₹28,000 crore
articles.summary: The board of directors of Tata Steel approved agreements on November 22, 2026, to sell its steel tubes and pipes business along with its entire stake in Tata Steel Colors Pvt Ltd to APL Apollo Tubes Ltd for a combined transaction value of approximately twenty-eight thousand crore rupees. Report author Imran Anati stated that emergency medical staff regularly face intimidation, threats at gunpoint, and physical violence from Israeli soldiers and settlers, creating severe obstacles for emergency responses and urgent patient care.
articles.description: Physicians for Human Rights Israel says medics face 'dangerous escalation' in violence from soldiers and settlers.

articles.headline: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones strike Russian warship in Libyan naval base
articles.title: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones hit Russian warship at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
articles.summary: Military officials reported that suspected Ukrainian sea drones struck the Russian Navy corvette Merkury at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya on November 22, 2026, causing a fire and explosion. Libyan authorities stated the vessel was docked for resupply under a bilateral agreement, while a joint investigation with Russia was launched to determine the source of the attack.
articles.description: The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said

articles.headline: Alice Huang maintained contact with Chinese intelligence during Nvidia affair
articles.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO, says NYT

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit concludes without consensus on new deal
articles.title: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?
articles.summary: The COP31 summit in Turkey officially ended without a consensus after participants rejected a fourth draft agreement. The European Union and other nations opposed the text because it failed to mandate a phase-out of fossil fuels, the primary driver of climate change. Negotiations broke down two days past their scheduled completion, marking the longest-running talks in the summit's history.
articles.description: The talks have been the longest-running in the summit's history, with negotiations breaking down two days after they had been due to end.

articles.headline: Seven-year-old boy rescued from rubble after Russian strikes in Ukraine
articles.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
articles.summary: Emergency crews pulled a seven-year-old boy and a 79-year-old woman from the wreckage of a residential building in Dymer after overnight Russian strikes killed ten people in the Kyiv region on Sunday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported that separate attacks across ten regions caused additional casualties, including three deaths in Vyshneve, as rescue operations continued amid ongoing air raid threats.
articles.description: Eleven people are dead in the attack on Dymer, with rescue efforts ongoing to find those still missing from the residential building.

articles.headline: BepiColombo spacecraft enters Mercury orbit amid reported thruster glitch
articles.title: Japan-Europe spacecraft BepiColombo begins orbit of Mercury, with a glitch reported
articles.summary: The European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency mission successfully placed the BepiColombo spacecraft into orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey. European Space Agency officials confirmed that a software issue caused a shorter-than-planned thruster burn during the orbital maneuver. The spacecraft remains safe as mission teams at the European Space Operations Centre investigate the anomaly ahead of planned separations.
articles.description: The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface

articles.headline: Russian missile strike kills two people and injures 60 in Kryvyi Rih
articles.title: Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown
articles.summary: An assault on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine resulted in multiple casualties after missiles struck residential buildings and medical facilities. Local officials reported that emergency workers were subsequently hit by secondary blasts during rescue operations. The military escalation comes amid ongoing international diplomatic efforts involving United States President Donald Trump and Ukrainian leaders to negotiate an end to the ongoing armed conflict.
articles.description: Attack on Kryvyi Rih comes as Russian missiles land in NATO member Poland and US-led peace efforts face uncertainty.

articles.headline: India administers over one crore HPV vaccine doses to girls
articles.title: HPV vaccination campaign: Every dose is step towards protecting girls from cervical cancer, says PM Modi
articles.summary: India reached a healthcare milestone by administering more than one crore single-dose HPV vaccines to 14-year-old girls under a national campaign in under nine months. Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated on November 23, 2026, that every dose protects girls from cervical cancer. According to the Health Ministry, the voluntary initiative has achieved nearly 87% of its annual target at designated government facilities.
articles.description: India has administered more than one crore doses of the HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls under its national vaccination campaign in less than nine months as on November 21

articles.headline: Nepal prime minister arrives in New Delhi for first official visit
articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah arrives in Delhi for first official visit to India
articles.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrived in New Delhi for his first official visit to India. During the trip, he is scheduled to hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to provide political direction to bilateral relations and inaugurate several infrastructure and connectivity projects across various sectors.
articles.description: The PMs of India and Nepal are set to hold talks on Monday, with sources saying the discussion will give 'political direction' to bilateral relations for the coming years

articles.headline: India and China conclude talks to ease border tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.summary: India and China concluded a second round of military talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh. The discussions, led by Lieutenant-General Girish Kalia and his Chinese counterpart, focused on establishing engagement protocols and preventing friction between deployed troops before the onset of harsh winter conditions.
articles.description: The talks focused on establishing engagement protocols, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, and maintaining open communication channels

articles.headline: Explosion damages Russian ship at Benghazi naval base in Libya
articles.title: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
articles.summary: An explosion occurred on a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base port following a suspected drone attack, according to Libya's eastern government. The incident happened at dawn while the vessel was stopping for fuel and supplies, prompting a joint investigation between local authorities and Russian counterparts.
articles.description: Libya's eastern government says the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia.

articles.headline: Anthropic shares decline on Nasdaq following record initial public offering
articles.title: Anthropic’s stock market debut: a record IPO, a quick fade, decabillionaires, and the risks ahead | Explained
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic launched its initial public offering on the Nasdaq on November 19, 2026, pricing shares at $83 before opening significantly higher at $111.50 and closing its debut at $97.17. The stock dropped 8.5 percent on its second trading day to close at $88.91 as trading volumes halved, highlighting investor questions regarding profitability and computing costs.
articles.description: The Claude maker’s shares surged on debut, valuing its founders’ stakes at billions, but soaring computing costs and the path to profitability remain key risks

articles.headline: Indonesian police recover 24 body bags after candy factory fire
articles.title: Indonesia confirms 24 killed in candy factory fire as search continues
articles.summary: Indonesian authorities are set to continue searching for 29 missing workers after police recovered 24 body bags from a gutted candy factory in Cikande, Serang regency. The fire broke out on Saturday evening at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia facility, where roughly 300 individuals were present. Officials noted that visual identification is impossible due to the fire's intensity, requiring DNA collection from relatives.
articles.description: Rescuers search for 30 people still missing.

articles.headline: US intelligence chief defends President Trump calling Vladimir Putin a friend
articles.title: US intelligence chief defends Trump’s comments calling Putin his ‘friend’
articles.summary: United States Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton defended President Donald Trump's description of Russian President Vladimir Putin as a friend during television appearances. Clayton asserted the language was appropriate for building personal rapport following a historic trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China. Meanwhile, critics and lawmakers raised concerns regarding United States foreign policy positions concerning Russia and Ukraine.
articles.description: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton says Trump's comments were 'entirely appropriate' in context of summit.

articles.headline: Poland confirms second Russian assassination attempt targeting Ukrainian rapper
articles.title: Poland says Russia tried to assassinate Ukrainian rapper twice
articles.summary: Polish and Danish authorities stated that Russian intelligence services targeted Ukrainian-American rapper Albert Vasiliev, known as Kyivstoner, in two separate assassination plots. Polish officials confirmed an August 2026 plot in Poland and the arrest of a suspect, while Denmark reported a September attempt near Copenhagen, leading to the expulsion of a Russian diplomat. Russia dismissed the allegations as unsubstantiated.
articles.description: Polish confirmation comes after Copenhagen reveals alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen on Danish soil.

articles.headline: WHO chief urges peace in DRC following heavy fighting near Ebola hospital
articles.title: WHO chief calls for peace amid heavy fighting in Ebola-hit DR Congo region
articles.summary: World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus appealed for an end to hostilities after clashes in Ituri province disrupted medical operations. Health personnel and relatives were forced to shelter in a maternity ward for over a day. As of November 17, the Democratic Republic of the Congo recorded 5,678 fatalities from 11,613 cases, representing the nation's largest outbreak while ongoing violence complicates relief delivery.
articles.description: Fighting near a DRC hospital disrupts Ebola efforts, putting patients and workers at 'grave risk', WHO warns.

articles.headline: South Korean stock market tumbles amid mounting fears over artificial intelligence bubble
articles.title: Asian stock markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount
articles.summary: Asian financial markets experienced sharp declines as investors worried about the long-term viability of the artificial intelligence boom. The Korea Composite Stock Price Index dropped as much as 3.2 percent in early trading on Monday, extending a regional sell-off that began at the end of the previous week. Japanese markets remained closed for Labour Thanksgiving Day during the trading session.
articles.description: Stocks fall in South Korea, mainland China and Hong Kong as tech sell-off deepens.

articles.headline: Trump criticises Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer amid upcoming leadership vote
articles.title: Trump criticises Schumer amid push for new Democrat leadership in US Senate
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump expressed opposition to Senator Chuck Schumer retaining his position as Senate majority leader in the incoming Congress. The debate highlights internal divisions within the Democratic Party following the November midterm elections. A closed-door ballot is scheduled for December 1, while Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is mounting a challenge against the incumbent New York lawmaker.
articles.description: Schumer, who has led the Democrats since 2017, faces a challenge from Chris Van Hollen in his bid for majority leader.

articles.headline: Polish territory struck by suspected Russian missiles and drone

articles.description: Warsaw accuses Moscow of intentional provocation, but bar for triggering NATO's collective defence clause remains high.

articles.headline: Rescue workers recover bodies after Russian strikes in Kyiv region

Emergency personnel successfully evacuated several residents earlier in the day amidst worsening security conditions.
articles.description: The BBC's Sarah Rainsford reports from the scene of a collapsed residential building in Ukraine's Kyiv region.

articles.headline: Democrats secure largest House majority since 1992 following North Carolina win

articles.headline: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot condemns settler attacks in West Bank
articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot denounced arson attacks and racist graffiti in Palestinian villages as Jewish terrorism, blaming the policies of ultra-nationalist cabinet ministers. Israeli police opened an investigation into the incidents while authorities grapple with an unresolved government formation process following recent elections.

articles.headline: Iran Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps downs two United States drones over Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says it downed US drones over Hormuz as bid to end war remains stalled
articles.summary: Iranian forces intercepted and shot down two United States drones over the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The incident occurred on Saturday amid ongoing military tensions and stalled diplomatic efforts to end the conflict. Meanwhile, the United States Treasury imposed new sanctions on four Iranian individuals accused of acting as oil trustees to evade maritime blockades.
articles.description: Iran reiterates conditions for Hormuz reopening as US slaps sanctions on four Iranians it says acted as 'oil trustees'.

articles.headline: Virginia reports first measles-related death of 2026 in child
articles.title: Virginia reports first measles-linked death of 2026 in child younger than 5
articles.summary: Virginia health authorities announced the state's first measles-related death of 2026 involving a child under five years old. The announcement arrived shortly after the United States lost its measles-free status, with national cases exceeding 5,800 this year. State officials confirmed 220 cases overall, predominantly among unvaccinated individuals, while federal agencies distribute additional funding to bolster vaccination and outbreak response efforts.
articles.description: The death comes within days of health experts stripping the US of its measles elimination status, amid uptick in cases.

articles.headline: Russian strike on Ukrainian apartment building kills two and wounds four
articles.title: Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes apartment building, killing two and wounding four others
articles.summary: Authorities reported that a Russian military strike destroyed a five-storey residential building in Dymer, located north of the Ukrainian capital, on November 22, 2026. Simultaneously, a rare air alert occurred in the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad following drone activity, while Finnish emergency services worked to extinguish a fire aboard a drifting Russian cargo ship.
articles.description: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble

articles.headline: Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties resume coalition talks in Israel
articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties resume talks to form Israel government
articles.summary: Delegations from Yashar and Likud met in Herzliya on November 22, 2026, to discuss forming a coalition government after recent elections failed to yield an absolute majority. articles.description: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government

articles.headline: Russian cargo vessel hit by drone attack in the Gulf of Finland
articles.title: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland
articles.summary: A cargo ship registered in Russia sustained damage and caught fire following an aerial drone strike while navigating through eastern maritime waters near Finland. Finnish defense forces indicated that Ukraine likely orchestrated the assault, which prompted temporary regional transit restrictions. Local authorities confirmed that the vessel's crew remained onboard to conduct necessary repairs, while regional officials monitored potential security implications stemming from the incident.
articles.description: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike on Saturday. Kyiv has yet to comment.

articles.headline: Securities regulators launch accounting investigation into artificial intelligence chip giant Nvidia
articles.title: Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media

articles.headline: U.S. court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in jail
articles.title: U.S. court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in jail in Pannun murder plot
articles.summary: A U.S. federal judge sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in prison on November 20, 2026. The 55-year-old pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire and money laundering charges related to a plot against Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. The verdict was delivered by Judge Victor Marrero in the Southern District of New York.
articles.description: Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty earlier this year to charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering, in connection with his efforts to murder Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York

articles.headline: Israeli settlers attack multiple Palestinian villages as pogroms surge
articles.title: Israeli settlers attack multiple Palestinian villages as pogroms surge
articles.description: Israeli settlers attacked several Palestinian towns and villages in the occupied West Bank on Sunday.

articles.headline: Drone attacks kill four people and damage United Nations building in Sudan
articles.title: Drone attacks kill four near Sudan’s capital, damage UN building
articles.summary: Drone attacks blamed on the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces killed four people in and around Khartoum while damaging a United Nations building. The strikes occurred as Sudanese air defences attempted to intercept drones targeting government installations, escalating concerns over civilian safety and the growing reliance on aerial weaponry in the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: The Rapid Support Forces are blamed as drones reportedly hit UN and government buildings, as well as Khartoum's airport.

articles.headline: Al Jazeera explores antibiotic overuse and antimicrobial resistance impacts
articles.title: The Drugs Don’t Work
articles.summary: A documentary examines how antimicrobial resistance could cause eight million annual deaths by 2050, focusing on infant mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. The film traces penicillin's history in the United Kingdom, explores pharmaceutical challenges at GlaxoSmithKline, and highlights academic research supported by DeepMind. Local innovations in Africa are also shown contributing to the global effort to combat resistant superbugs.
articles.description: A look at how antibiotic overuse could fuel superbugs, killing eight million people annually by 2050.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy urges United States to approve Patriot missile deliveries
articles.title: Zelenskyy urges US to release Patriot missiles as Russia kills 7 in Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on Washington to release paid Patriot interceptor systems following intense Russian aerial bombardments across twenty regions that killed five people near Kyiv and in Zaporizhzhia. According to officials, recent strikes damaged infrastructure including a grocery store, a cargo ship, and an electricity facility. Meanwhile, Russia's Ministry of Defence claimed control of Sosnovyi Bir, though claims remained unverified.
articles.description: Three Russian attacks kill at least six people near Kyiv as overnight Russian shelling kills one in Zaporizhzhia.

articles.headline: Bangladesh deploys paramilitary troops following deadly political protests and unrest
articles.title: Why Bangladesh descended into violence ahead of Hasina’s planned return
articles.summary: Bangladesh deployed ninety additional platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh after political violence resulted in four deaths and numerous arson attacks across twenty-eight districts. Unrest erupted following government rejection of a passport request for exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who was previously sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity related to the 2024 student protests.
articles.description: Supporters of ousted PM, who lives in self-imposed exile in India, have protested against rejection of her return.

articles.headline: Drone strikes damage residential homes and United Nations premises in Khartoum
articles.title: Drone strikes hit homes, UN premises in Sudan's capital
articles.summary: Unidentified drone strikes hit residential areas and a United Nations building in the Sudanese capital of Khartoum on November 22, 2026. A Sudanese Army source claimed the drones originated from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport, a charge previously denied by Addis Ababa. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs condemned the attacks, which occurred amid an ongoing civil conflict between the army and the Rapid Support Forces.
articles.description: A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese Army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia

articles.headline: Russian missile violates Polish airspace during military exercises
articles.title: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
articles.summary: Poland reported that a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that breached its airspace on Friday during major aerial attacks on Ukraine. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incursion as a provocation coinciding with Western military exercises. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned the grave violations, confirming that alliance jets were scrambled in response to the ongoing regional conflict.
articles.description: Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi drone and missile as Sanaa fuel station is hit
articles.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts drone, missile as Houthis report attack on Sanaa
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi drone and missile targeting Riyadh and the Red Sea coast on November 22, 2026. Meanwhile, Houthi-affiliated media reported that air strikes in Sanaa injured six employees at a state-run fuel station. The escalation follows recent Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and ongoing clashes between the internationally recognised Yemeni government and the armed group.
articles.description: Houthi media say several people were injured in an attack on an oil company as Saudi air defences down a drone.

articles.headline: Gaza children with diabetes face severe insulin shortages and surging medication prices
articles.title: Children in besieged Gaza struggle to find life-saving insulin for diabetes
articles.summary: Children with type 1 diabetes in the Gaza Strip are experiencing severe health complications due to critical shortages and skyrocketing prices of insulin and blood glucose testing strips. Driven by the ongoing Israeli siege and widespread unemployment, families struggle to afford essential medications, forcing some to rely on expired supplies and resulting in life-threatening hospital admissions for severe blood acidity.
articles.description: Insulin and blood glucose testing supplies become increasingly difficult to obtain in war-torn Gaza.

articles.headline: US Democrats plan to leverage funding bill to end Iran war
articles.title: US Congress helped end the Vietnam War. Can it stop the Iran war?
articles.summary: Democratic lawmakers are preparing to block a critical government funding package due by December 11 unless it includes provisions to restrict President Donald Trump from using federal money for offensive operations in Iran. Supporters argue this strategy mirrors the approach used by Congress to end the Vietnam War by cutting off financial military support.
articles.description: Congress forbade funding for the Vietnam War, contributing to the fall of the South Vietnamese government in Saigon.

articles.headline: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian villages in occupied West Bank
articles.title: Israeli settlers attack several Palestinian villages in occupied West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli settlers burned 12 vehicles and vandalized homes in the Ramallah and el-Bireh provinces of the occupied West Bank early Sunday. The Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission reported a 112 percent increase in settler attacks during October. Israeli military officials have launched an investigation into the incidents, which Gadi Eisenkot labeled as Jewish terrorism.
articles.description: Attacks in Ramallah, el-Bireh provinces included the burning of 12 vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on homes.

articles.headline: Iran intensifies military attacks on tankers and US bases
articles.title: What’s behind Iran’s escalation of attacks in the Gulf?
articles.summary: Iran has escalated regional hostilities by targeting tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and claiming strikes on US military bases in Bahrain. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated these actions respond to US sanctions and airspace violations. The conflict has significantly disrupted global oil shipping, causing insurance premiums to rise and supply volumes to drop.
articles.description: Tehran has ramped up attacks as the US naval blockade and sanctions campaign hurt the country economically.

articles.headline: Russian ship attacked by drone in Baltic Sea off Finland
articles.title: Russian ship attacked by drone in Baltic Sea off Finland
articles.description: Russian ship attacked by drone in Baltic Sea off Finland

articles.headline: Russian drone strike collapses apartment building in Ukraine's Kyiv region
articles.title: At least 14 people missing after Russian drone hit building in Kyiv region, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary: At least fourteen people remain missing under the rubble after a Russian drone struck a residential building on Sunday in Ukraine's Kyiv region, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Nine individuals were successfully evacuated while local officials reported two injuries. Emergency services continue rescue operations following the collapse of the five-story structure.
articles.description: Emergency ‌service footage showed rescuers ​searching through a large pile of ⁠rubble, helping residents descend ⁠from the damaged building by ‌ladder and crane platform

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts ballistic missile over western region
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missile in western region
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition announced on Sunday that air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Houthi militia toward Saudi Arabia's western Red Sea coast. Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki confirmed the attack targeting the region containing critical energy infrastructure. Recent strikes by the group have caused casualties and damaged prominent facilities.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia's western region contains key energy infrastructure including the Yanbu terminal, a major facility for crude oil exports

articles.headline: South Korean education minister resigns over AI cheating scandal
articles.title: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
articles.summary: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned, taking full responsibility for exam security confusion during the Suneung college entrance test. President Lee Jae Myung accepted the resignation following a confession by Han Won-seok, who admitted using a microcamera and artificial intelligence tools. Authorities deployed emergency mobile alerts and strict anti-cheating protocols across South Korea after discovering 111 candidates with unauthorised smart devices.
articles.description: Choi Kyo-jin admits last-minute measures to stop AI-assisted cheating during the college entrance exam caused chaos.

articles.headline: ‘Trump’s exit strategy may depend on quietly lifting Iran blockade’
articles.title: ‘Trump’s exit strategy may depend on quietly lifting Iran blockade’
articles.description: US President Donald Trump will have to ease the naval blockade on Iran if he wants the war to wind down, says analyst.

articles.headline: Dashcam captures Russian missile strike on Lviv, Ukraine
articles.title: Dashcam captures Russian missile strike on Lviv, Ukraine
articles.description: Dashcam video captured the moment a missile struck a residential neighbourhood in Lviv, western Ukraine.

articles.headline: Max Verstappen wins the Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time
articles.title: Max Verstappen wins the Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time in four years
articles.summary: Red Bull driver Max Verstappen secured victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 22, 2026, holding off competitors during a race featuring thirty-five lead changes. Starting from pole position, Verstappen triumphed after early battles with George Russell and late pressure from Lando Norris. Oscar Piastri finished third, while Russell crashed near the end to take ninth place.
articles.description: Verstappen started from the pole position, but was under pressure from the start before pulling away from Norris, the 2025 series champion, on the final lap. Oscar Piastri finished third and current champ Antonelli fourth

articles.headline: Somalia expels Emirati ambassador and recalls envoy from Abu Dhabi
articles.title: Why Somalia’s president turned against his former ally, the UAE
articles.summary: Somalia ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador to leave Mogadishu on November 19, 2026, and recalled its own envoy following the annulment of several bilateral agreements. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused Abu Dhabi of undermining national security and financing regional rivals. The diplomatic rupture stems from escalating tensions over federal authority and regional administrations.
articles.description: Behind Somalia's break with the UAE lies a domestic power struggle with regional leaders close to Abu Dhabi.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit faces delays as co-hosts release new draft agreement
articles.title: New draft deal aims to avert collapse of talks at COP31 climate summit
articles.summary: Negotiators at the United Nation COP31 summit in Antalya faced further delays on November 22, 2026, after co-hosts Turkey and Australia released a revised draft agreement. The text omits explicit calls to transition away from fossil fuels, drawing criticism from the European Union. Turkey Environment Minister Murat Kurum expressed hope for a breakthrough despite ongoing disputes over finance and targets.
articles.description: The UN COP31 meeting in Turkey enters a second day of overtime as countries struggle to reach an agreement.

articles.headline: COP31 final draft agreement omits specific mention of fossil fuels
articles.title: COP31: Turkiye's final draft doesn't mention the words ‘fossil fuels’ that cause global warming
articles.summary: Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum released the latest draft agreement for the COP31 summit in Antalya on November 22, 2026, omitting any reference to fossil fuels. The text includes a controversial goal for carbon capture and storage while addressing clean energy consumption targets. Delegates received limited time to review the proposal as negotiations stretched into overtime.
articles.description: COP31 President Murat Kurum gave negotiators only about three hours to make objections or ask for changes before the wording goes before the conference plenary

articles.headline: United States restricts remote access to advanced AI chips for Chinese firms
articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.summary: The United States Commerce Department introduced new regulations on November 17, 2026, to prevent Chinese companies from accessing advanced AI chips via data centres in third-party nations. The rule mandates export licenses for semiconductors sent to countries like Malaysia and Singapore. Beijing condemned the move, accusing Washington of abusing export controls to hinder China's technological development.
articles.description: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

articles.headline: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge and oil facilities as Putin and Trump meet in Shenzhen
articles.title: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge as Putin ally declares ‘no one needs Europe’
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces launched a multi-day operation targeting the Kerch Bridge, damaging its road and rail sections, while also striking oil depots and the Rostov-Crimea highway to disrupt Russian supply lines. Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on November 19, discussing peace proposals regarding Ukraine and European security architecture.
articles.description: Russia-Europe tensions rise as Ukraine uses its own weapons and communications tech to hit the Kerch Bridge.

articles.headline: COP31 climate talks enter overtime as Turkish officials propose fossil fuel text
articles.title: COP31 climate talks on the brink as new draft deal faces scrutiny
articles.summary: Negotiators at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya extended discussions into a second day of overtime after Turkish officials introduced a last-minute compromise addressing fossil fuels. Murat Kurum, the Turkish environment minister and summit president, stated the conference would reconvene to approve the deal following intense consultations between Australia, Turkiye, and nearly 200 delegations.
articles.description: New draft would acknowledge for the first time that global ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠warming is on course to pass the 1.5C threshold.

articles.headline: Russian president compares Shenzhen trilateral summit to 1945 Yalta Conference
articles.title: The Shenzhen trilateral | The unlikely trio
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin drew comparisons between a recent trilateral summit with American and Chinese leaders in Shenzhen and the 1945 Yalta Conference. Speaking to the press on November 19, 2026, Putin suggested that codifying a victory over neo-Nazism would be appropriate, similar to how the historic Crimean summit involving Soviet, American, and British leaders shaped the post-war European political order.
articles.description: Leaders of the U.S., Russia and China agreed to begin talks on nuclear risk reduction but offered no details on institutionalising the dialogue process

articles.headline: International Court of Justice rules Myanmar committed Rohingya genocide
articles.title: The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted people
articles.summary: In a historic ruling, the International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingya during military clearance operations in Rakhine State in 2017. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate perpetrators, ensure non-repetition, and allow the safe return of displaced persons. The final judgment resulted from a case brought by The Gambia in 2019.
articles.description: The International Court of Justice’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during its 2017 ‘clearance operations’ offers a measure of justice for the ethnic and religious minority, but the court has no means of enforcing its judgment

articles.headline: Displaced Palestinians protest in Gaza as Israeli strikes and home destructions continue
articles.title: Displaced Palestinians protest as Israeli air strikes continue in Gaza
articles.summary: Hundreds of displaced residents demonstrated near Deir el-Balah to protest against intensifying air strikes and property destructions by Israeli forces beyond the Yellow Line established under a ceasefire. According to local officials, recent attacks have left hundreds of thousands homeless, while continuing military operations and recent strikes have caused numerous casualties across the enclave.
articles.description: Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings as part of a 'gradual displacement' policy, a Gaza mayor says.

articles.headline: Thousands march in Lisbon to protest soaring living costs and housing crisis
articles.title: Thousands march in Lisbon as living costs fuel anger
articles.summary: Thousands of individuals participated in a central Lisbon march on November 21, 2026, organised by trade union federation CGTP to protest against increasing living costs, low wages, and a severe housing crisis. Protesters demanded higher wages and lower prices. Portugal faces high inflation and surging property prices, compounding economic pressures experienced by workers and younger generations across the country.
articles.description: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing

articles.headline: Mexican special forces arrest top FBI most-wanted drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores
articles.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
articles.summary: Mexican special forces detained alleged drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Guasave, Sinaloa, following a shoot-out involving gunfire and explosives. Meza Flores, leader of the Meza Flores Organisation and on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, was flown to Mexico City to face extradition and prosecution. The operation occurred amid increased Mexican efforts to combat cartels under US pressure.
articles.description: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.

articles.headline: Russian missile strikes target Kyiv bridges and kill six people
articles.title: Russia targets Kyiv crossings days after Ukraine hits Crimean Bridge
articles.summary: Russia launched nearly one hundred missiles and four hundred drones targeting Ukrainian infrastructure, hitting three Dnipro River bridges in Kyiv and killing six individuals. Additional strikes in Lviv claimed two lives at a railway station, while Polish forces investigated a projectile landing near the border. Officials reported widespread injuries, power disruptions, and ongoing air raid sirens across nine regions.
articles.description: Russia launched one of its biggest air attacks yet as it rejected the prospect of security guarantees for Ukraine.

articles.headline: Clashes erupt across France in another night of protest
articles.title: Clashes erupt across France in another night of protest
articles.description: French police charged to disperse crowds on Saturday as the country faced a sixth weekend of demonstrations.

articles.headline: Federal Bureau of Investigation investigates apparent hack of criminal information database
articles.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
articles.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center database, according to United States media reports citing two briefed sources. The database is utilized by law enforcement agencies to share information regarding warrants and background checks. This development follows recent high-profile cybersecurity incidents and the firing of White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross.
articles.description: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.

articles.headline: U.S. Commerce Department issues interim rule restricting advanced AI chip exports
articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department issued an interim final rule on November 16, 2026, barring foreign data centers with American AI chips from providing cloud services to businesses in twenty-four countries, including China, Iran, and Russia. China criticized the move as an overreach of national security, while the policy builds on export controls established in 2018.
articles.description: The U.S. Commerce Department on November 16 issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside the U.S. equipped with advanced American AI chips from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia

articles.headline: Lebanese president demands Israeli withdrawal and condemns Iranian interference
articles.title: Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
articles.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun criticized Iranian meddling and demanded a full Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon in a speech ahead of the country's independence anniversary. According to authorities, ongoing Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon have killed thousands of people since fighting began. Aoun also pledged to bring all armed groups under state control.
articles.description: Joseph Aoun says 'two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked' mean Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit deadlocked over fossil fuel reduction references
articles.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
articles.summary: Negotiations at the COP31 United Nations climate summit in Turkey entered a deadlock after a group of nations led by France and Panama opposed a draft agreement omitting references to reducing fossil fuel demand. Disagreements also persist over funding for adaptation, with African nations demanding increased financial support. A new agreement is anticipated as discussions continue among participating international ministers.
articles.description: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.

articles.headline: Russia targets Ukrainian infrastructure and bridges in retaliatory air attacks
articles.title: Russia unleashes retaliatory barrage on Kyiv bridges
articles.summary: Russian air attacks killed eight people and struck transport bridges and energy infrastructure across Ukraine. Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi reported 28 injuries following the overnight strikes. President Vladimir Putin ordered the retaliation after a bridge linking Russia to Crimea was targeted. Meanwhile, US-led ceasefire efforts continue as officials discuss security guarantees and NATO positions.
articles.description: The attack follows Putin's pledge of 'painful' response to Ukraine's attack on symbolic Crimean bridge.

articles.headline: Bahrain reports industrial facility fire following Iranian aerial attack
articles.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack caused fire at industrial facility
articles.summary: Bahrain announced that an Iranian aerial attack struck a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire but no injuries, according to the Bahrain Defence Force and the Ministry of Interior. Meanwhile, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it targeted United States military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases in response to airspace violations. The incident occurred amid escalating regional conflict involving Gulf Arab states and Iran.
articles.description: Bahrain reports no injuries as Iran's IRGC says it targeted US military positions at two bases in al-Riffa and Awali.

articles.headline: Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot invites Likud party for coalition talks
articles.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for Israeli coalition talks
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming the next Israeli government, invited caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party for coalition talks beginning on Sunday, November 22, 2026. The centrist Yashar party leader stated the meetings reflect a commitment to forming a broad government. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett expressed opposition to joining Netanyahu's bloc.
articles.description: ‘In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow’ read a statement

articles.headline: Iran urges US to accept conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says held talks with Qatari mediators, urges US to accept conditions
articles.summary: Iranian officials met with Qatari mediators in Tehran to discuss terms for reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz, according to state media. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Washington must accept conditions including the lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the economic blockade before shipping lanes can be restored following the conflict that began on February 28.
articles.description: Iran's foreign minister says reopening the strait is 'not difficult' if the US accepts reasonable conditions.
