articles.headline: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya population
articles.title: What does the ICJ’s Rohingya genocide ruling mean for Gaza?
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice in The Hague has delivered a historic verdict ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its minority Rohingya population. United Nations judges found that security forces carried out widespread atrocities, including killings and sexual violence. Legal experts note the landmark ruling could potentially influence South Africa's ongoing genocide case against Israel at the court regarding the conflict in Gaza.
articles.description: The case sets a precedent for establishing a state's intent to commit genocide beyond explicitly written orders.

articles.headline: US military tightens naval blockade on Iranian cargo transfers
articles.title: US targets Iran’s ship-to-ship transfers: Can Tehran break the blockade?
articles.summary: The United States military announced that vessels receiving Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers will face potential military action and enforcement measures. United States Central Command stated the advisory aims to close loopholes allowing petroleum exports to bypass existing blockades. Analysts warn the escalation could provoke Iranian retaliation against regional energy infrastructure and increase wider geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.
articles.description: CENTCOM declares vessels bypassing the Iran blockade could be stopped, boarded or even seized by US forces.

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu plea over Cauvery water release
articles.title: Cauvery dispute: SC dismisses Tamil Nadu plea on Karnataka not making good shortfall in water share
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 20, 2026, dismissed an application from Tamil Nadu claiming a shortfall of 11.719 thousand million cubic feet in Cauvery water flows from Billigundulu. A Bench led by Justice Vikram Nath delivered the judgment after Karnataka opposed the request, arguing that the Cauvery Water Management Authority had not ordered the release.
articles.description: The judgment is based on applications filed by T.N., alleging that Karnataka had failed to implement the binding judgment of the SC to ensure water to to TN at Billigundulu on a pro-rata basis during distress years like the current one

articles.headline: Young Nigerians face financial and political barriers in upcoming elections
articles.title: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
articles.summary: Abdulhadi Dalhatu is among the young candidates running for office in Nigeria's upcoming general elections in January. Although about eighty percent of the population is under forty, high nomination fees and campaign costs hinder youth participation. Major political parties have set steep fees, while voter registration among citizens under thirty-five has declined.
articles.description: Fewer young people have registered to vote in next year's election than in 2023 - are young people losing faith in democracy?

articles.headline: Teen gamer and mother help rescue missing girl held in Oregon
articles.title: How a teen gamer and his mother helped rescue a missing girl
articles.summary: Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp and his mother Khristina helped rescue a seventeen-year-old girl who had been missing for over a year. After chatting online, the victim revealed she was held against her will by Adam Hunter Harmel in Oregon. Khristina located the address using property records and coordinated with the Federal Bureau of Investigation to secure her release.
articles.description: When 16-year-old Landon Tresp met a teenage girl in an online game, it led to him and his mother helping the FBI rescue her from kidnapping.

articles.headline: ‘We didn’t come here to beg’: Africa’s message at COP31
articles.title: ‘We didn’t come here to beg’: Africa’s message at COP31
articles.description: Ghana has demanded climate justice and funding for African nations, warning COP31 leaders against empty promises.

articles.headline: European Union and United Kingdom reach post-Brexit policy agreements
articles.title: ‘The deal is done’: EU, UK agree to reset relations 10 years after Brexit
articles.summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom sealed agreements covering youth mobility, sanitary regulations, and emissions trading systems following a Brussels summit. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated the deals will benefit both economies, though domestic critics condemned the arrangements. Implementation will require legal processes in each country as both sides pursue a broader reset in relations.
articles.description: Deals on food and animal goods, mobility and student fees have been agreed, but months of negotiations lay ahead.

articles.headline: Indonesian wildfires cause economic losses exceeding thirty billion dollars
articles.title: Economic losses from Indonesia fires could reach $30 billion, research shows
articles.summary: Severe wildfires across Indonesia have destroyed 2.88 million hectares of land this year, generating economic losses and health costs estimated at over thirty billion dollars. According to research from the Center of Economic and Law Studies published on November 20, 2026, asset damages and respiratory illness treatment expenses accounted for the total. Researchers attribute the intensified fire season to climate change, deforestation, and El Nino weather patterns.
articles.description: Wildfires have burned through 7.1 million acres so far in 2026, according to the Nusantara Atlas deforestation monitor, an area 18 times the size of London

articles.headline: US envoy Jared Kushner says Russia is comfortable with NATO-like security pact for Ukraine
articles.title: Kushner says Russia OK with ‘NATO-like’ security pact for Ukraine: Is it?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump's envoy Jared Kushner stated that Russia is comfortable with post-war security guarantees for Ukraine modeled on NATO Article 5. Speaking in Berlin alongside European leaders, Kushner indicated Trump is open to the package. Meanwhile, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov rejected any form of quasi-membership for Kyiv, highlighting ongoing tensions over Ukraine's 2022 NATO application.
articles.description: NATO Article 5 says attack on one member is an attack on all. Analysts say inclusion of Ukraine 'stretches credulity'.

articles.headline: Malaysia plans to resettle 10000 Rohingya refugees in Turkiye
articles.title: Malaysia plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkiye
articles.summary: Malaysia plans to resettle 10000 Rohingya refugees in Turkiye through a structured skills training programme. Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced the Cabinet decision following the International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the ethnic minority. The initiative aims to provide vocational training and employment opportunities for refugees, who make up two-thirds of Myanmar asylum seekers in Malaysia.
articles.description: The announcement by Deputy PM Ahmad Zahid Hamidi comes a day after the UN's top court, in a landmark ruling, said that Myanmar committed genocide against the ethnic minority

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi criticizes corporate India over domestic manufacturing progress
articles.title: Why is PM Modi upset with corporate India? | Explained
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry leaders, criticizing the domestic industry for failing to enhance manufacturing since the 1930s. Speaking on November 19, 2026, the leader highlighted economic concerns that have frequently been raised by the political opposition, lending additional institutional weight to these longstanding structural issues.
articles.description: The Prime Minister pulled up industry leaders on four different issues. Government data and anecdotal evidence shows why he is angry

articles.headline: Rohingya refugees welcome United Nations court ruling on Myanmar genocide
articles.title: Rohingya in Bangladesh welcome UN court’s genocide verdict but say they want to go home to Myanmar
articles.summary: Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar camp welcomed the International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during military operations. The legally binding judgment ordered reparations and safe returns for refugees, though implementation challenges remain. Approximately one million two hundred thousand displaced individuals currently reside in crowded Bangladeshi camps.
articles.description: “The Rohingya have their own distinct culture, their own language, their own land and everything else that defines an ethnic group,” said a Rohingya community leader

articles.headline: India and Bulgaria review bilateral ties and regional security during talks
articles.title: India, Bulgaria discuss bilateral ties, IMEC, Black Sea situation
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Bulgarian counterpart Velislava Petrova met at Hyderabad House in Delhi on November 22, 2026, to assess cooperation across trade, security, and technology. The officials also discussed connectivity projects including the India Middle East Europe Economic Corridor, alongside the Ukraine conflict and the Black Sea situation, aiming to strengthen broader diplomatic and economic exchanges.
articles.description: ‘Our teams have drawn up a detailed roadmap of cooperation, so we will be approving that today, and I think that will give a very clear pathway to our activities ahead,’ said S. Jaishankar

articles.headline: Myanmar calls UN court genocide ruling unfair and unjust
articles.title: Myanmar calls ICJ ruling on genocide 'unfair'
articles.summary: Government spokesperson Khaing Khaing Soe stated that the United Nations International Court of Justice ruling was unfair and that Myanmar was unjustly accused. The court found Myanmar responsible for state-sponsored genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. Judges highlighted mass executions and sexual violence during clearance operations. articles.title: Pakistan minister visits India for first time since 2025 war
articles.summary: Musadik Malik arrived in New Delhi to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum, marking the first visit by a Pakistani federal minister since a brief war in May 2025. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to inaugurate the gathering. Both governments framed the visit as routine multilateral business, with no bilateral meetings currently scheduled between the two nuclear-armed neighbours.
articles.description: Islamabad and New Delhi insist the visit is strictly multilateral, despite hopes it could open a channel for contact.

articles.headline: Former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro hospitalized in intensive care
articles.title: Brazil’s Jair Bolsonaro in intensive care with bowel obstruction
articles.summary: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro was admitted to the DF Star hospital in intensive care after being diagnosed with an acute bowel obstruction. The 71-year-old, who is currently serving a 27-year prison sentence for an attempted coup, is clinically stable and receiving fluids and nutritional support. Bolsonaro has faced recurring health issues and numerous surgeries following a 2018 campaign stabbing.
articles.description: The former president, serving a sentence for plotting a coup, is stable and breathing on his own, the hospital says.

articles.headline: Thousands protest across Europe over living costs and housing
articles.title: Thousands protest across Europe over living costs and housing
articles.summary: Thousands of demonstrators marched across France and Portugal to demand higher wages, affordable relief, and action against soaring property prices. In France, the Ministry of Interior reported tens of thousands of participants in nationwide gatherings. The demonstrations followed separate student and worker protests in Germany, Sweden, and Italy concerning economic insecurity and public service funding.
articles.description: Demonstrations in France and Portugal follow youth-led protests over education and economic hardship across Europe.

articles.headline: AOC challenged over AIPAC’s influence on Democratic leadership
articles.title: AOC challenged over AIPAC’s influence on Democratic leadership
articles.description: US Representative AOC was challenged by an activist over her support for Hakeem Jeffries, in light of his ties to AIPAC.

articles.headline: El Salvador president launches controversial third term re-election campaign
articles.title: El Salvador’s Bukele seeks third term after constitution change
articles.summary: El Salvador President Nayib Bukele officially registered his candidacy for the February elections following constitutional changes by his party Nuevas Ideas that removed term limits. While popular due to a gang crackdown, critics and human rights organizations accused the forty-five-year-old populist of consolidating power, packing courts, and creating a de facto one-party state.
articles.description: Critics accuse populist president of engineering a de facto one-party state in El Salvador.

articles.headline: US Army plans controlled detonations of lead-rich explosives in Iowa
articles.title: Why is the US Army detonating lead-rich explosives in Iowa?
articles.summary: The United States Army intends to destroy sixty-eight drums of degraded lead azide at an installation in Middletown, Iowa. The operation was authorized by an emergency United States Environmental Protection Agency permit, but prompted legal challenges from environmental groups and criticism from local officials over potential health risks and insufficient public notice prior to the scheduled blasts.
articles.description: The delayed blasts have stoked environmental fears and concerns about health effects in the state.

articles.headline: Doctors warn against hazardous fairness creams after teenager develops kidney ailment
articles.title: Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder
articles.summary: Medical professionals in Keralam's Malappuram district revealed on Friday that a 17-year-old girl was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy after using an online fairness cream containing mercury. Experts attribute the incident to unregulated online beauty products promoted by social media influencers. Consequently, the Keralam Drugs Control department launched student awareness campaigns and market inspections to prevent further heavy metal poisoning cases.
articles.description: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early

articles.headline: White House fires cyber chief Sean Cairncross amid outages
articles.title: White House fires cybersecurity chief after widespread outages
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump administration dismissed cyber security chief Sean Cairncross following widespread communication and travel outages, a source told Agence France-Presse on November 19, 2026. Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies will fill the role in an acting capacity. State Secretary Marco Rubio congratulated Davies on X, as concerns persist over artificial intelligence threats and credential requirements.
articles.description: Sean Cairncross’ role will be filled in an acting capacity by current Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi calls for government action against the narcotics trade
articles.title: PM Modi calls for sustained government drive against drug trade, stresses financial prudence
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged a sustained government campaign to eliminate the narcotics trade during a review meeting with his Council of Ministers. Following the ASEAN summit, the Prime Minister also emphasized financial prudence among citizens and cited World Bank findings showing five hundred million people lifted out of poverty.
articles.description: At a review meeting with his Council of Ministers, the Prime Minister also assessed progress in poverty reduction and the elimination of left-wing extremism

articles.headline: Noni Madueke secures draw for Arsenal against Newcastle United
articles.title: Noni Madueke salvages draw for Arsenal at Newcastle United as Raya injured
articles.summary: Arsenal missed an opportunity to extend their lead in the Premier League after a second-half comeback from Newcastle United resulted in a two-all draw. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke scored for the defending champions, while Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw responded for the hosts. Additionally, goalkeeper David Raya suffered an injury during the match.
articles.description: League leaders Arsenal miss the chance to go eight points clear of second placed Brighton, who play on Sunday.

articles.headline: Kerala High Court remarks trigger renewed debate over Kochi nightlife and safety
articles.title: Kerala High Court’s remarks trigger fresh debate on Kochi’s night life
articles.summary: Recent Kerala High Court remarks questioning police crackdowns on DJ parties have revived discussions regarding Kochi's night culture. District Police Chief R. Nishanthini stated restrictions target drug-related crimes, while Mayor V.K. Minimol defended nightlife as a necessity for stressed citizens. Stakeholders and merchant representatives emphasized balancing public enjoyment with safety and transportation measures.
articles.description: Court’s question on whether the police are opposed to nightlife altogether sparks debate over the city’s growing appetite for late-night events and gatherings and long-standing concerns raised by law enforcers

articles.headline: J&K job aspirants launch indefinite strike in Srinagar over recruitment board cheating scam
articles.title: Amid cold wave, students’ indefinite strike against J&K recruitment board scam gathers steam
articles.summary: Protesting government job aspirants launched an indefinite strike in Srinagar during freezing temperatures over irregularities in the Jammu and Kashmir Service Selection Board examinations. articles.description: ‘Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will; the demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA rigging; this fight isn’t over,’ said a protester

articles.headline: Historian Ramachandra Guha discusses ideological opposition to Gandhi in India
articles.title: Gandhi is the core ideological enemy of the Sangh Parivar: Ramachandra Guha
articles.summary: Historian Ramachandra Guha stated that Mahatma Gandhi has become the primary ideological enemy of the right-wing Sangh Parivar ecosystem. Speaking alongside author B. Jeyamohan, Dr. Guha noted that while early post-independence India venerated Gandhi, contemporary right-wing groups display intense detestation due to his non-violent policies and advocacy for inter-faith harmony.

articles.headline: Cyclone Arnab triggers deadly landslides across multiple Odisha districts
articles.title: Eastern Ghats on a slippery slope
articles.summary: Torrential rain from Cyclone Arnab caused devastating landslides in Odisha, destroying villages such as Gidipabali and Dangeshi and displacing residents. According to Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari, 17 people have died across 92 landslides in six districts this year, with Kandhamal recording the highest number of incidents at 59, severely disrupting regional connectivity and tribal livelihoods.
articles.description: The deaths of 10 people in two landslides triggered by Cyclone Arnab have drawn attention to the fragile ecology of the Eastern Ghats in Odisha and the growing dangers lurking in its hills. Satyasundar Barik examines how climate extremes, deforestation, and unplanned development are threatening the ecosystem

articles.headline: Retired bureaucrat questions dissolution of Union-State relations committee
articles.title: T.N. govt. gave no advance notice on Justice Kurian panel’s dissolution: member
articles.summary: Retired civil servant K. Ashok Vardhan Shetty stated that members received no advance warning before the dissolution of the committee on Union-State relations. Mr. Shetty questioned the decision to transfer pending responsibilities to the State Law Commission, noting that the panel lacked prior experience with federal matters and policy issues.

articles.headline: UK and EU expected to agree on youth mobility scheme
articles.title: UK and EU to agree youth mobility scheme, BBC understands
articles.summary: Up to one hundred thousand young people from the European Union and the United Kingdom could gain the ability to travel, work, and study in each other's territories annually under an upcoming agreement negotiated ahead of a Brussels summit. According to the BBC, discussions are continuing regarding caps and fees while officials aim to finalize broader packages covering food trade rules and immigration enforcement.
articles.description: The scheme is expected to be approved at Friday's UK-EU summit, with new deals on food trade and carbon emissions also on the table.

articles.headline: British and European Union leaders to meet for summit
articles.title: EU and Britain to agree steps towards relations reset
articles.summary: British and European Union leaders are scheduled to meet in Brussels to discuss steps toward resetting relations a decade after the Brexit vote. articles.headline: Kannada writer Ravi Hanj detained at Kochi airport over book
articles.title: Kannada writer Ravi Hanj tracked to Kochi airport, served notice to appear for probe amid Basava Mantapa book controversy
articles.summary: Kannada writer Ravi Hanj was detained by Central Industrial Security Force personnel at Cochin International Airport during security checks while attempting to travel abroad. articles.description: Ravi Hanj was detained during security checks while attempting to travel abroad, say Kerala Police sources.

articles.headline: Trade unions and farm outfits demand Prime Minister Narendra Modi reverse economic policies
articles.title: Reverse policies, stop tax sops for rich: Trade unions, farm outfits to PM Modi
articles.summary: Trade unions and farmers' organisations demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi apologise for the failure of Make in India and Viksit Bharat 2047 projects. articles.description: Referring to the PM’s remarks at the recently-held Annual General Meeting of FCCI, farmers’ unions and trade groups say employment generation remains low despite tax cuts and incentives to corporate companies

articles.headline: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino prepares for Premier League match against Liverpool
articles.title: Liverpool vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
articles.summary: Manchester United begins a new era under manager Mauricio Pochettino when they face Liverpool at Anfield in the English Premier League on Sunday, November 22, 2026. articles.description: One of sport's biggest rivalries takes centre stage as Liverpool host a Man United side in the EPL relegation zone.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi addresses platinum jubilee celebrations at IIT Kharagpur
articles.title: Break free of limiting beliefs to achieve new heights: PM Modi at IIT Kharagpur
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged students to abandon limiting beliefs during the platinum jubilee celebrations of the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur on November 21, 2026. Institute director Professor Suman Chakraborty announced a five million dollar donation from alumnus Sundar Pichai for artificial intelligence research.
articles.description: Narendra Modi joins Platinum Jubilee celebrations of the first IIT of the country and says the institute has and will continue to play a major role in nation building

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav launches new political slogan ahead of Uttar Pradesh Assembly election
articles.title: ‘Lathi haregi-Laptop jitega’: Akhilesh coins slogan aimed at youth, pushing development pitch
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav introduced the slogan Lathi haregi-Laptop jitega on November 21, 2026, promoting a development-focused agenda. The former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister highlighted his previous laptop distribution scheme for students and accused the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party of relying on fear and conservative policies, while alleging that certain state officials are acting as party functionaries.
articles.description: SP says slogan echoes the popular sentiment of GenZ in U.P., which is fed up with the BJP’s ‘bulldozer raj’ and the unscientific agenda of the RSS being imposed over the Constitution and the rule of law

articles.headline: Karnataka Cabinet orders forfeiture of copies of Ravi Hanj book Basava Mantapa
articles.title: Is forfeiting copies of a book the right way to handle ‘objectionable content’?
articles.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet decided to forfeit copies of the book Basava Mantapa by NRI author Ravi Hanj over alleged derogatory remarks about social reformer Basavanna, reigniting debate over freedom of expression and public order. articles.headline: History of world chess championships and legendary players examined
articles.title: World chess championship: Genuises who wielded their magic
articles.summary: Emanuel Lasker held the record as the longest-reigning world chess champion for twenty-seven years, beginning in 1894 when he defeated Wilhelm Steinitz in New York, Philadelphia, and Montreal. According to The Hindu, Lasker was also a mathematician and philosopher. His reign ended in 1921 against Jose Raul Capablanca. Subsequent champions included Alexander Alekhine and Max Euwe before Alekhine died holding the title in 1946.

articles.headline: IndusInd Bank terminates former chief Sumant Kathpalia and invokes clawbacks
articles.title: IndusInd Bank terminates Sumant Kathpalia’s services, invokes clawback provisions
articles.summary: IndusInd Bank terminated the services of former Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Sumant Kathpalia with immediate effect following disciplinary proceedings. The bank board acted on an inquiry report submitted by a former Bombay High Court judge on November 18, 2026. The private sector lender also invoked malus and clawback provisions dating back to March 24, 2020, following earlier disclosures regarding accounting lapses and derivative portfolio discrepancies.
articles.description: The bank’s board acted on an inquiry report by a former Bombay High Court judge and invoked malus and clawback provisions from March 24, 2020

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi stresses importance of skilled youth at Lucknow convocation
articles.title: World needs skilled youth, not merely degree-holders, says PM Modi
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that the world requires skilled youth rather than solely degree-holders during the fifth Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow on November 21, 2026. Speaking at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, he emphasized that Industrial Training Institute graduates contribute directly to nation-building and deserve equal respect to engineering students. He highlighted the establishment of nearly 5,000 new institutes since 2014 and honoured top-performing students.
articles.description: ITI students deserve the same respect as IIT students, he says at ITIs convocation ceremony; the skills acquired at ITIs are not merely a means of securing employment but also an opportunity to participate directly in nation-building, PM Modi says

articles.headline: Indian plastics industry aims to double export volume within four years

Taparia announced the target at the PLEXCONNECT 2026 conference in Mumbai, highlighting manufacturing capabilities, new free trade agreements, and expanding markets in Africa and Latin America.

articles.headline: Indian supply chains have 500 billion dollars in trapped inventory

articles.summary: Razat Gaurav, chief executive officer of Canadian software firm Kinaxis, stated during a Mumbai conference that approximately 500 billion dollars in inventory remains trapped within Indian supply chains. Gaurav noted that quick commerce presents modern fulfillment challenges while Kinaxis continues providing planning software to companies like Mahindra, Sun Pharma, and Tata Consumer Products across India.
articles.description: Quick commerce is adding complexity to supply-chain planning, while AI agents could allow companies to do the same work with fewer employees, though workforce reduction is not the primary objective, says Razat Gaurav

articles.headline: Hafele aims for fifty percent local sourcing and sustained double-digit growth in India
articles.title: Hafele targets 50% localisation in India, eyes sustained double-digit growth
articles.summary: Home interiors solutions provider Hafele India has increased its local sourcing to over thirty percent and plans to reach fifty percent over the next few years. Frank Schloeder, managing director of Hafele South Asia, stated that the firm is investing two hundred crore rupees in a new manufacturing unit in Maharashtra. The company reported revenue of approximately one thousand two hundred crore rupees in 2025.
articles.description: The premium German home and kitchen solution brand plans to broaden its living solutions portfolio and strengthen its presence across India’s home interiors market says Hafele South Asia MD Frank Schloeder.

articles.headline: Lam Research enters commercial supply discussions with Indian semiconductor fabrication players
articles.title: Lam Research intensifies focus on Indian semiconductor mart as local fab discussions gather momentum
articles.summary: Lam Research is in active talks with Tata Group and other emerging companies to supply fabrication equipment for upcoming fabs in India. The initiative aims to build domestic capabilities and address workforce training gaps through the Semiverse virtual platform.
articles.description: Despite India’s large pool of mechanical, electrical, chemical and software engineering graduates, the semiconductor industry faces a shortage of people with practical knowledge of fabrication processes, says Lam Research India head Rangesh Raghavan

articles.headline: Google grants five million dollars to IIT Kharagpur for artificial intelligence research
articles.title: Google offers $5 mn to IIT Kharagpur for AI research, talent development
articles.summary: Google announced a five million dollar funding package for the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur to support advanced artificial intelligence research and technical talent development. The collaboration aims to strengthen India's technological ecosystem and academic capabilities.
articles.description: Building AI that works for everyone requires deep collaboration and strong academic leadership, says Google

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi blames Manipur government negligence for sixteen toxic liquor deaths
articles.title: Manipur hooch deaths: Rahul Gandhi blames negligence of BJP government
articles.summary: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi condemned the Bharatiya Janata Party government in Manipur following sixteen deaths attributed to spurious liquor consumption. Manipur police reported approximately 600 hospitalisations in Chandel district since November 18. articles.description: In a post, he says violence devastated hundreds of homes and now toxic liquor is wreaking havoc while the government remains asleep

articles.headline: India defeats South Korea 2-1 in women's Asian Champions Trophy
articles.title: India huffs and puffs past a stubborn South Korea in the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy hockey
articles.summary: Sjoerd Marijne's Indian side secured a 2-1 victory over South Korea at the International Sports Complex on Saturday, propelled by goals from Mumtaz Khan and Sunelita Toppo. articles.headline: Indian opposition youth wing protests against Meta over account removals
articles.title: India’s opposition stages protests against Meta over account removals
articles.summary: Members of the Indian Youth Congress staged demonstrations outside Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai, and Gurugram on Friday and Saturday, demanding the restoration of restricted Instagram accounts. articles.headline: Indian officials arrive in Dhaka for Joint River Commission meeting

articles.description: A Joint Committee under the Joint River Commission will meet on November 22-23, while it is not clear if the Commission has the mandate to renew the treaty

articles.headline: Mexican special forces arrest top fugitive cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores
articles.title: Who is El Chapo Isidro, the alleged cartel boss arrested in Mexico?
articles.summary: Mexican special forces detained Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, an alleged cartel leader featured on the Federal Bureau of Investigation's ten most wanted fugitives list, during a Friday night operation in Guasave, Sinaloa. articles.headline: Teenager hacks Agniveer recruitment test website using artificial intelligence tools

Investigators recovered data from his devices and contacted the National Informatics Centre to determine what information was compromised.
articles.description: The Haryana teenager used an AI chatbot to identify valuable data and find a way into the test portal; preliminary investigation suggests only names and addresses were accessed, Delhi Police sources say

articles.headline: India administers over one crore HPV vaccine doses to girls
articles.title: HPV vaccination: one crore doses administered in nine months
articles.summary: India distributed over one million human papillomavirus vaccine doses to 14-year-old girls in under nine months under a campaign launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February. According to the Health Ministry, six states achieved full coverage, utilising the U-WIN platform for monitoring as part of efforts to prevent cervical cancer.
articles.description: Nearly 87% of its annual target cohort of 14-year-old girls has been covered under the national cervical cancer prevention campaign. Uttar Pradesh leads with more than 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar (13.70 lakh) and Gujarat (7.75 lakh)

articles.headline: Kashmir religious leader welcomes Pakistani minister visiting India for forum
articles.title: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq hails Pakistan accepting India’s SCO invite, terms it ‘positive step’
articles.summary: Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq welcomed Pakistan Climate Minister Musadik Masood Malik attending the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Cultural Dialogue Forum in New Delhi on November 21, 2026. The visit follows strained ties after a 2025 conflict. Local politicians described the development as a positive step toward resuming bilateral dialogue on shared concerns including climate change and political issues.
articles.description: Ties between India and Pakistan nosedived after the Pahalgam attack triggered a war between the two neighbours in 2025

articles.headline: Democrats prepare to assume control of United States Congress in January
articles.title: US midterms 2026: What happens before the new Congress takes office?
articles.summary: Following midterm elections, Democrats secured control of both houses of the United States Congress, though Republicans retain majority powers during the lame-duck session until January 3, 2027. Lawmakers face an upcoming December 11 government funding deadline. Once in power, Democratic majorities will gain committee authority and subpoena power while navigating potential legislative vetoes from President Donald Trump.
articles.description: What happens between the US midterm elections and January, when Democrats take control of Congress?

articles.headline: French presidential candidate blames media for racist attack
articles.title: French presidential candidate blames media for racist attack
articles.description: French presidential candidate blames media for racist attack

articles.headline: United States court sends summonses to Indian officials in lawsuit
articles.title: U.S. court dispatches summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun case
articles.summary: A United States court dispatched summonses to Indian National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and former intelligence director Samant Goel regarding a civil lawsuit filed by separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. The legal action seeks damages over an alleged assassination plot, which the Indian government has rejected as fabricated and malicious.
articles.description: The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts designated by notification of the Central Government of India to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts

articles.headline: Journalist Sashi Kumar stresses importance of free media
articles.title: Free media key to democracy: Sashi Kumar
articles.summary: A free media is essential for maintaining a true democracy, according to journalist Sashi Kumar during a keynote address at a seminar organized by the Kerala State Human Rights Commission. Kumar stated that the media currently faces an existential crisis due to credibility erosion, corporate influence, and political pressure. Kerala Assembly Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan also emphasized the need for self-regulation on social media platforms during the event.
articles.description: Assembly mulling setting aside a day for people to ask authorities questions, says Assembly Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan at SHRC seminar on free speech and Fourth Estate

articles.headline: Bengaluru protest restrictions at Freedom Park restrict public dissent, says report
articles.title: Report documents impact of restrictions on the right to protest in Bengaluru
articles.summary: A study by PUCL-Karnataka and published by the Campaign for the Right to Protest reveals that the 2021 Licensing Order confining demonstrations to Freedom Park in Bengaluru has rendered public dissent invisible and led to arbitrary police detentions. Released by Justice H. N. Nagamohan Das, the report documents multiple instances of police high-handedness against activists and workers, noting that these regulations severely burden civic freedoms.
articles.description: The report by PUCL-Karnataka highlights how the restriction has rendered protests invisible to the public and has had cascading impact on those who seek State accountability

articles.headline: Karnataka cabinet approves distribution of 15 lakh free residential sites
articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet clears 15 lakh free sites, one lakh houses
articles.summary: The Karnataka cabinet chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar approved distributing fifteen lakh free residential sites and building one lakh houses for ₹2,241 crore. The initiative includes the Bhooguarantee and Niveshana Yojane schemes prioritizing vulnerable groups. Eligible citizens must hold specific ration cards and meet income limits for online applications verified using Aadhaar data.
articles.description: The decisions were taken at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 19

articles.headline: Karnataka chief minister leads delegation to Japan for investment and urban planning
articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister to lead delegation to Japan for investment talks, urban-planning study
articles.summary: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar is heading a high-level Karnataka delegation to Japan from November 23 to 25 to secure new investments and examine advanced urban management systems. Accompanied by Industries Minister M.B. Patil and officials from the Greater Bengaluru Authority, the group will visit Nagoya, Osaka, and Tokyo to meet corporate leaders and study transit-oriented development and waste management.
articles.description: The visit will focus on two areas: attracting fresh investments from Japanese companies and understanding Japan’s approach to urban planning, transport, waste management and infrastructure development

articles.headline: India joins global ocean alliance and commits to expand marine monitoring
articles.title: India joins global ocean alliance, pledges to double Indian Ocean monitoring
articles.summary: India has officially joined the Ocean Eye International Alliance for the Global Ocean Observing System during the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkiye. Represented by T.M. Balakrishnan Nair, director of the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services, India pledged to double its observation network across the Indian Ocean to improve climate resilience, weather forecasts, and marine safety.

articles.headline: Yadadri Thermal Power Station ash pollutes Telangana stream
articles.title: Yadadri Thermal Power Plant: The toxic cost of power
articles.summary: Residents of Veerlapalem village in Telangana's Nalgonda district raised concerns over ash slurry pollution in the Thungapahad stream caused by the Yadadri Thermal Power Station. Farmer V. Nageshwar Rao filed a complaint with the Telangana Pollution Control Board in May 2026, prompting a show-cause notice issued to the Telangana Power Generation Corporation Limited the following month.
articles.description: Fly ash from the 4,000-MW Yadadri thermal plant is polluting a stream that sustains farms and fishing communities, before flowing into the Krishna river. As Telangana powers up, the fallout extends beyond the vicinity of the project, which started operations less than two years ago, with concerns rising over water quality, public health and livelihoods along the river system, reports Swathi Vadlamudi

articles.headline: India and Finland seek to strengthen economic ties through startup collaboration
articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.summary: Ambassador Mikko Kivikoski stated that India and Finland aim to deepen bilateral economic cooperation by connecting their startup ecosystems and boosting investments. Speaking in New Delhi during the Polar Bear Pitching event, where Yash Goliya emerged as the winner, the envoy highlighted growing diplomatic engagements and noted that bilateral trade reached approximately 3.7 billion dollars in 2025-26.
articles.description: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

articles.headline: Banu Mushtaq calls for wider translations of Kannada works; Mallika Ghanti calls for end to poornakumbha practice involving girl students
articles.title: Banu Mushtaq calls for wider translations of Kannada works; Mallika Ghanti calls for end to poornakumbha practice involving girl students
articles.description: Literature enables people to look beyond their personal experiences and understand the emotions and struggles of others, noted author and winner of the International Booker Prize Banu Mushtaq, on Thursday

articles.headline: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju rejects religious discrimination claims over cricketer selection
articles.title: Nobody in India faces religious discrimination: Rijiju amid Siraj row
articles.summary: Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju and Uttar Pradesh Bharatiya Janata Party leaders dismissed allegations by Congress MP Imran Masood that bowler Mohammed Siraj was dropped from the Test squad against New Zealand due to his religion. Officials stated selections rely strictly on merit, while critics accused the opposition of promoting polarisation ahead of state elections.
articles.description: The remarks of the Minister and BJP leaders came after Masood, the MP from Saharanpur and U.P. Congress working president, allegedly said that Siraj was not given a place in the side because of his name

articles.headline: Parliament's Monsoon session remains unprorogued for 100 days, government yet to announce special sitting
articles.title: Parliament's Monsoon session remains unprorogued for 100 days, government yet to announce special sitting
articles.description: Both Houses were adjourned sine die (for an indefinite period) on August 13, but neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha has been prorogued (formal conclusion of session) as of November 21 morning

articles.headline: PM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu bridge and development projects in Bihar
articles.title: PM Modi inaugurates bridge named after Nitish Kumar in Bihar’s Vaishali
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi formally inaugurated the 9.76-kilometre cable-stayed bridge over the river Ganga, named Nitish Setu, connecting Kacchi Dargah and Bidupur. Constructed for over 5,500 crore rupees, the inauguration occurred on November 21, 2026, alongside foundation stone laying for projects worth 34,470 crore rupees. The event drew criticism from opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav regarding the bridge's naming and previous construction history.
articles.description: The bridge connects Kachhi Dargah on National Highway 22 in Patna district with Bidupur on NH-322 in Vaishali. It comprises a 9.76-km main bridge and 10 km of approach roads, officials said

articles.headline: Florida residents turn to kayaks and rafts as floods swamp streets
articles.title: Florida residents turn to kayaks and rafts as floods swamp streets
articles.description: Days of heavy rain have flooded streets across Florida, forcing residents to find creative ways to get around.

articles.headline: Telangana government issues guidelines for Indiramma family life insurance scheme
articles.title: Telangana issues guidelines for ₹5 lakh Indiramma family life insurance scheme; permits only one application per ration card
articles.summary: The Telangana government released enrolment guidelines for the Indiramma Kutumba Jeevitha Bima Padhakam, offering five lakh rupees in life insurance to one earning member per eligible household. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy launched the scheme in Siddipet. A month-long rural and urban enrolment drive requires Aadhaar and ration cards for applicants aged eighteen to fifty-nine years.
articles.description: Telangana government will undertake a month-long enrolment drive through special camps at the gram panchayat level in rural areas and designated wards in urban areas

articles.headline: Adani Defence successfully demonstrates Bagheera anti-tank missile system in Pokhran
articles.title: Adani Defence fires four anti-tank missiles in Pokhran Test Range
articles.summary: Adani Defence and Aerospace successfully tested its Bagheera AT1 vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile system at the Pokhran Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan. Representatives from the Indian Army and Ministry of Defence witnessed the November demonstration. Developed over eighteen months, the system features automated launchers mounted on high-mobility armoured vehicles to enhance combat capabilities.
articles.description: The missile is capable of engaging armour at up to 8 km, twice the approximately 4 km range of the land-based anti-tank missile

articles.headline: Why is GTA VI so expensive to play?
articles.title: Why is GTA VI so expensive to play?
articles.description: Grand Theft Auto VI costs less than GTA V to buy, yet far more to play. AJLabs explains where the money goes.

articles.headline: Pakistan Cricket Board drops former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood
articles.title: Pakistan drop Rizwan and Masood, but back Babar and Agha in overhaul
articles.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board removed former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood from central contracts during an extensive overhaul expanding the contracted player pool to thirty-eight. Announced following a Test series victory against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi, the new system runs until June 2027 and features five specialized categories for players.
articles.description: Former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood lose Pakistan central contracts, but Babar Azam and Salman Agha backed.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav alleges government officials are working as BJP functionaries in Uttar Pradesh
articles.title: Some government officials working as 'BJP functionaries' ahead of Uttar Pradesh polls: Akhilesh Yadav
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav alleged that certain government officials and police personnel are acting as Bharatiya Janata Party functionaries ahead of the elections. During a Lucknow press conference, he confirmed ongoing seat-sharing discussions with Congress and criticized the administration on voter roll issues, corruption, and constitutional governance challenges.
articles.description: Akhilesh Yadav said discussions are under way with the Congress on seat-sharing and his party would suggest constituencies where the Congress had a chance of winning

articles.headline: Convicts lawyer rejects Bilkis Bano suppression claims over bail
articles.title: Convicts’ lawyer rejects claims of Bilkis Bano being kept in dark, warns against media trial
articles.summary: Advocate Ayush Anand, representing two convicts granted bail by the Supreme Court in the 2002 Bilkis Bano case, dismissed allegations that the survivor was kept uninformed about legal proceedings. The rebuttal followed a public statement by Ms. Bano alleging she was not heard before the October 28 bail order. The lawyer stated the matter was listed ten times over a year, with notices issued in March.
articles.description: Supreme Court’s order for the duo’s release on bail came in an appeal filed by them against a 2017 Bombay High Court judgment upholding a CBI court decision of 2008, convicting the men and sentencing them to life terms in prison

articles.headline: Congress launches Uttar Pradesh OBC outreach campaign demanding caste census
articles.title: Countering ‘latecomer’ tag, Congress sharpens caste census pitch in Uttar Pradesh
articles.summary: Seeking to counter perceptions that it is late to engage backward classes, the Congress party announced a series of conventions in Uttar Pradesh to push for a caste census. According to AICC OBC Department National Chairman Anil Jaihind, the party advocates for proportional representation and intends to challenge the twenty-seven percent reservation cap once enumeration data is released. He also noted that Rahul Gandhi is expected to address upcoming December events.
articles.description: On the absence of OBC leaders in the party’s top leadership in U.P., Anil Jaihind said Rahul Gandhi was keen to introduce dedicated grassroots workers into the organisational pipeline as district presidents and AICC secretaries, and to allow the best to flourish

articles.headline: Migrants caravan in Mexico walks towards US border
articles.title: Migrants caravan in Mexico walks towards US border
articles.description: Around 300 migrants have crossed from Guatemala into Mexico, hoping to reach the United States.

articles.headline: Rajasthan panchayat election results expose gaps in ruling BJP rural support
articles.title: BJP’s urban gains fail to win rural support in Rajasthan panchayat polls
articles.summary: The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party faced significant electoral setbacks in rural Rajasthan panchayat polls despite previous success in urban local body elections. Seventeen state ministers and three Union ministers failed to defend their local political strongholds. The opposition Congress secured major gains by winning hundreds of zila parishad and panchayat samiti seats, highlighting stark contrasts between urban and rural voter sentiment across the state.
articles.description: The outcome is particularly significant as several BJP ministers faced electoral setbacks in their areas of influence

articles.headline: Deadly fire engulfs power station in southern Iraq
articles.title: Deadly fire engulfs power station in southern Iraq
articles.description: At least four people were killed and 30 injured after a fire tore through the Hartha power station complex.

articles.headline: Padmaja Venugopal's exit from BJP reignites tensions in Thrissur Congress
articles.title: Padmaja’s BJP exit reopens old wounds in Congress
articles.summary: Padmaja Venugopal has resigned from the Bharatiya Janata Party, citing personal reasons after joining the party in March 2024 following her departure from the Indian National Congress. Her resignation has triggered resistance among local Congress leaders in Thrissur regarding her potential homecoming, reopening old factional disputes stemming from her past allegations of internal sabotage during her election campaigns.
articles.description: BJP calls her resignation unfortunate, citing personal reasons for her decision; Suresh Gopi, Thrissur MP, distances himself from her induction into BJP; Congress leaders voice opposition to her possible return

articles.headline: Israeli army issues demolition notices for residential buildings in Hebron
articles.title: Demolition notices for buildings in Hebron provoke fear among Palestinians
articles.summary: The Israeli army issued demolition notices for two multi-storey residential buildings in the Dairat al-Seer area of Hebron, citing security proximity to a settler road. Located in Area A under Palestinian control, the properties house dozens of families who possess municipal permits. Property owners have submitted legal objections, as the community faces severe anxiety and potential displacement from the military orders.
articles.description: Palestinians fear forced displacement as Israeli authorities target legally licensed homes in West Bank.

articles.headline: Mehbooba Mufti urges Amit Shah to investigate Kashmiri youth death
articles.title: Mehbooba Mufti urges Amit Shah to ensure thorough probe into Kashmiri youth’s death in Amritsar
articles.summary: People's Democratic Party president Mehbooba Mufti urged Union Home Minister Amit Shah and the Punjab police chief to conduct a time-bound investigation into the murder of a twenty-seven-year-old Kashmiri man named Aijaz Ahmed Dar. The victim from Kokernag went missing on September 23, and his body was discovered in Amritsar on October 28. Although two arrests have been made, the family continues seeking justice according to the party leader.
articles.description: She said while two persons have been arrested, the family still awaits justice

articles.headline: New AICC in-charge faces challenges during maiden visit to Hyderabad
articles.title: New AICC in-charge B.M. Sandeep to face challenges in Telangana Congress on his maiden visit
articles.summary: Newly appointed All India Congress Committee secretary in-charge of Telangana, B.M. Sandeep, faces internal party dissent during his first visit to Hyderabad on November 22, 2026. The ruling Congress government is confronting public criticism from legislators including Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy and Anirudh Reddy regarding the distribution of development funds and ministerial resource allocation, prompting intervention from party leadership to restore discipline.
articles.description: Telangana Congress MLAs are openly criticising the government, senior Ministers over disproportioonate fund allocations

articles.headline: Data reveals private sector hospital births reach record high via C-section
articles.title: Study shows most births in private sector hospitals are taking place via C-section
articles.summary: Corporate employee health insurance claims analyzed by Plum Data Labs show that the average rate of Caesarean section births in private hospitals reached 69 percent. According to Chief Technology Officer Saurabh Arora, clinical factors and hospital choices drive high rates, while 82 percent of insured families still pay out of pocket because median claims exceed standard policy limits.
articles.description: Interestingly, the data showed that the percentage of C-sections in Tamil Nadu (39% in Chennai, 27% in Coimbatore, 20% in Madurai), where mothers give birth earlier, was lower than in Mumbai, the Delhi-NCR and Bengaluru, where nearly 60% of mothers are 30 or older

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu approves additional infrastructure funding for urban local bodies
articles.title: Tamil Nadu government clears another ₹387 crore for urban infrastructure works
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government approved one thousand six hundred four infrastructure projects worth three hundred eighty-six crore rupees for 2026-27, covering road improvements, water supply, parks, and crematoriums across municipalities, corporations, and town panchayats. The package was sanctioned during an October meeting and formalised through orders issued on November 18 by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department under the Chief Minister Integrated Urban Development Mission.
articles.description: Of the total projects approved, the majority relates to roads; 1,540 road works have been approved across Tamil Nadu

articles.headline: Bangladesh minister vows strict action against arson and petrol bomb attacks
articles.title: Bangladesh Minister vows action against those behind arson, blames Awami League-linked groups, says reports
articles.summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated that Bangladesh will pursue strict legal action against individuals responsible for recent arson and petrol bomb attacks, attributing the violence to groups linked to the banned Awami League. Speaking on November 20, 2026, the minister alleged that exiled leadership is instigating unrest and confirmed that former prime minister Sheikh Hasina will be sought exclusively through extradition treaties.
articles.description: Humaiun Kobir said law enforcement agencies were working to bring those responsible to justice and alleged that the Awami League’s leadership, including those based abroad, was encouraging the attacks

articles.headline: UK-EU deal proceeds independently of tuition fees agreement, Ed Miliband says
articles.title: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
articles.summary: British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband confirmed to the BBC on Sunday that the recently agreed cooperation pact with the European Union will take effect in 2028 regardless of a separate tuition fees agreement. The Brussels deal includes reduced checks on British food exports and a youth mobility scheme, though opposition leaders criticized the terms and economic projections.
articles.description: Brussels sources had previously suggested the bloc might not apply the wider deal until fees were lowered for EU students in Britain.

articles.headline: Kerala Pradesh Mahila Congress demands resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.title: Kerala Pradesh Mahila Congress stages ‘Kerala Jantar Mantar’ protest outside Lok Bhavan demanding resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: The Kerala Pradesh Mahila Congress staged a protest outside the Keralam Lok Bhavan demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the electoral roll revision. State leaders condemned the actions of national officials and vowed to continue defending the Constitution. Participants included AICC general secretary Deepa Dasmunsi and Mahila Congress president Jebi Mather.
articles.description: Deepa Dasmunsi, AICC general secretary in charge of the State, said Congress party will continue with its protests until Gyanesh Kumar resigns as CEC

articles.headline: Cricket Australia expresses unanimous support for Test captain Pat Cummins
articles.title: Sandpapergate: Cummins has Australia’s ‘unanimous support’ as Test captain
articles.summary: Cricket Australia confirmed its unanimous backing for Test captain Pat Cummins despite controversy over the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal. Board chairman David Boon rejected claims regarding Cummins and announced a new player forum. Teammate Josh Hazlewood defended Cummins while expressing potential doubts about his own future should the captain face removal from his post.
articles.description: Pat Cummins to remain Test captain after Cricket Australia back cricketer following cheating scandal in South Africa.

articles.headline: Independent SIR commission asks Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister for voter data
articles.title: Independent SIR Commission asks CM Adityanath for proof of his statement that 1.27 crore Hindus excluded
articles.summary: The Independent Commission on the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls wrote to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath requesting supporting material for his statement that 1.27 crore Hindus were excluded from the voters list. Chaired by former Supreme Court judge Justice Madan B. Lokur, the civil society initiative seeks data to examine potential methodology gaps during the revision exercise.
articles.description: In its letter to the Chief Minister, the Commission said his statement was directly relevant to its mandate of examining whether eligible electors were unfairly removed from the rolls during the SIR exercise

articles.headline: French court finds three police officers guilty of racially motivated assault
articles.title: French police officers guilty of Michel Zecler assault: What happens now?
articles.summary: A Paris criminal court convicted three police officers of intentional racist violence and falsifying reports during the 2020 assault of music producer Michel Zecler. The defendants received five-year prison sentences with varying suspended portions and permanent bans from the force. The incident drew renewed scrutiny regarding systemic brutality and discrimination within French law enforcement agencies.
articles.description: Officers dealt more than 30 blows to the Black music producer in what the court ruled was a racially motivated crime.

articles.headline: Harry Kane to miss few months after tearing ankle ligament
articles.title: Harry Kane to miss ‘a few months’ after injury as Bayern Munich draw
articles.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane will sidelined for several months following a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle. The injury occurred during a 1-1 draw against Cologne when defender Joel Schmied collided with him. The outcome leaves the Bundesliga leaders without their key forward as they maintain their position at the top of the table.
articles.description: Ballon d'Or winner tears a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne.

articles.headline: Fourteen flights cancelled at Ranchi airport due to cyclone Akvan
articles.title: 14 flights cancelled at Ranchi airport due to bad weather triggered by cyclone 'Akvan'
articles.summary: Fourteen scheduled flights were cancelled at Birsa Munda Airport in Ranchi on November 21, 2026, due to inclement weather caused by cyclone Akvan. Airport Director Vinod Kumar reported visibility dropped to around one thousand metres. The cyclone brought cloudy weather and light rain to Jharkhand, falling short of the required twelve hundred metres visibility needed for safe aircraft operations.
articles.description: Jharkhand has been experiencing cloudy weather coupled with light rain since November 21 under the influence of the cyclone

articles.headline: Swimmer braves tanker attacks to expose Hormuz contamination
articles.title: Swimmer braves tanker attacks to expose Hormuz contamination
articles.description: As tankers burned in Hormuz, swimmer Lewis Pugh exposed another casualty of the US-Israeli war on Iran: marine life.

articles.headline: Union Home Minister Amit Shah addresses Siang Valley dam project concerns
articles.title: Concerns of people of Siang Valley over dam project to be addressed through dialogue: Shah
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated that concerns of people in Arunachal Pradesh regarding the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project will be addressed through dialogue. Speaking at Banderdewa, he assured that local culture, traditions, and religious beliefs will remain protected while advancing the hydroelectricity initiative. He also noted positive security changes in Jammu and Kashmir since the abrogation of Article 370.
articles.description: The Union Home Minister said he has learnt about people's concerns through the media and acknowledged that many of the issues raised by them were significant

articles.headline: Kerala hospitals face clinical psychologist shortage for disability certificates
articles.title: Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates
articles.summary: People with intellectual disabilities in Kerala face difficulties obtaining and renewing certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals for Intelligence Quotient assessment tests. Union government guidelines require differently abled children to undergo assessments multiple times before age 18. Only 22 clinical psychologists operate under the Directorate of Health Services and the Directorate of Medical Education combined.
articles.description: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

articles.headline: Supreme Court refers Central Secretariat Library relocation matter to Chief Justice
articles.title: What is the controversy over the relocation of the Central Secretariat Library? | Explained
articles.summary: The Supreme Court referred the relocation controversy surrounding the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library to the Chief Justice of India for an appropriate bench assignment. Originally housed in the Shastri Bhawan complex, the library was ordered to vacate for the Central Vista redevelopment project without a designated new space. The court previously took suo motu cognisance and sought a detailed government affidavit.

articles.headline: Supreme Court stresses protection of Central Secretariat Library books
articles.title: Heritage is not just Lutyens, but also books at the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library, SC tells government
articles.summary: The Supreme Court told the Union government that cultural heritage extends to protecting centuries-old books at the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library in Shastri Bhawan. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta assured the Bench led by Justice Sanjay Kumar that the government stands by its November 16 undertaking not to shift the books from their current premises during redevelopment.
articles.description: Centre says it values the books as a treasure; the library has tomes dating back to 1702

articles.headline: Justice B.V. Nagarathna delivers inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Oxford
articles.title: Full text of the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture delivered by Supreme Court Justice B.V. Nagarathna
articles.summary: Supreme Court Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated on Wednesday that women occupying high public offices does not prove societal equality has been achieved. Delivering the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Somerville College, she traced the historical evolution of women's legal status in India from feudal protection to constitutional rights and professional inclusion.
articles.description: Only the practice of substantive equality could take care of these differences among women hailing from and living through diverse life experiences, the Judge said.

articles.headline: EPFO approves systematic withdrawal plan for periodic retirement payouts
articles.title: What does EPFO’s Systematic Withdrawal Plan entail for retirees | Explained
articles.summary: The Central Board of Trustees of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation approved a systematic withdrawal plan on November 19, 2026, in New Delhi. Retiring members can now choose monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or annual payouts instead of taking a lump sum. The remaining corpus stays invested to earn interest, while members gain flexible options to enhance savings through voluntary contributions.
articles.description: As per the proposed SWP, upon retirement or superannuation, a member will have several options to receive the accumulated PF corpus or a part through periodic withdrawals instead of a lump-sum withdrawal

articles.headline: Can mediation succeed in a war-torn world? | Episode 1
articles.title: Can mediation succeed in a war-torn world? | Episode 1
articles.description: With more than 65 armed conflicts raging worldwide, top mediators reveal why peace has never been harder to achieve.

articles.headline: Blaze at Hartha power station in Iraq kills four people
articles.title: At least four killed, 35 injured in fire at power station in Iraq’s Basra
articles.summary: A fire at the Hartha power station in southern Iraq killed at least four individuals and injured thirty-five others, according to Iraqi state media reports. The Iraqi News Agency stated that civil defence teams controlled the blaze, which forced operations to stop at the 800-megawatt facility and damaged neighbouring houses on November 21, 2026.
articles.description: The blaze erupted at the Hartha power station and spread to nearby houses.

articles.headline: Honduran court convicts four individuals in connection with woman disappearance
articles.title: Three US citizens among 4 convicted in Honduras over sex-trafficking case
articles.summary: A court in Honduras convicted four people on November 20, 2026, of criminal association linked to the 2022 disappearance of university student Angie Pena. The Public Ministry stated it will request maximum ten-year sentences for United States citizens Harold Green, William James Murdock, and Gary Lee Johnston, alongside Honduran national Gustavo Trejo, while appealing human trafficking acquittals.
articles.description: The defendants face 10 years in jail after being found guilty of recruiting women into a sex-trafficking ring.

articles.headline: Scientists predict La Niña conditions could strengthen India's 2027 monsoon season
articles.title: After strong El Niño, La Niña may boost India’s 2027 monsoon, says INCOIS forecast
articles.summary: Researchers at the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services in Hyderabad reported that the current El Niño weather pattern will likely persist until March. Climate models suggest a subsequent shift toward neutral conditions and a growing probability of La Niña emerging to potentially enhance rainfall during the Southwest Monsoon in 2027.
articles.description: Scientists indicate that the ongoing strong El Niño could persist until March 2027, followed by neutral conditions and a possible transition to La Niña during the Southwest Monsoon. They are also monitoring widespread marine heatwaves across the Indian Ocean

articles.headline: Congress criticizes government over delimitation bill and parliamentary majority
articles.title: PM, HM still searching for ‘supertainted’ two-thirds majority for delimitation bill, says Congress
articles.summary: The Congress party stated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah remain focused on securing a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha for a delimitation bill. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh argued that current parliamentary configurations and reservations for women should remain frozen until achieving the Viksit Bharat objective.
articles.description: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and state-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented till the Viksit Bharat objective is achieved

articles.headline: K.L. Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal lead India to 239/1 at lunch
articles.title: IND vs NZ, 1st Test: India end Day 3 on 486/4, lead by 118
articles.summary: K.L. Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal advanced India's first-innings score to 239 for one at lunch on the third day of the first Test against New Zealand at Basin Reserve, trailing by 129 runs. Rahul reached 93 not out while Padikkal contributed an unbeaten 53, adding 80 runs during the morning session under clear skies and a breeze, leaving Rahul seven runs shy of his 13th Test hundred.
articles.description: India amassed 327 runs in 86 overs to finish the third day at 486/4. That gave it a lead of 118 runs, with two days remaining

articles.headline: Pune startup QuPrayog develops laboratory-scale atomic clock prototype
articles.title: Pune startup develops atomic clock prototype amid growing export curbs on critical technologies
articles.summary: Pune-based startup QuPrayog Private Limited built a Rubidium-87 atomic clock prototype using Coherent Population Trapping technology within seven months. Chief executive officer Jay Mangaonkar stated the project aims to reduce reliance on imported timing systems amid export controls, supporting India's National Quantum Mission and indigenous capabilities.
articles.description: Atomic clocks are critical to satellite navigation, telecommunications, space missions and strategic systems, where highly precise and stable timekeeping is essential.

articles.headline: Montek Singh Ahluwalia says States must drive next economic reforms phase
articles.title: States must drive next phase of reforms, says Montek Singh Ahluwalia
articles.summary: Former Planning Commission deputy chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia stated on Friday at a conference in Hyderabad that India's next economic reforms must rely on State-level policies. Speaking at the Public Policy 2026 event, he emphasized that advanced States like Gujarat and Maharashtra must grow faster to help achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047, while addressing land acquisition and urban infrastructure.

articles.headline: Kiren Rijiju questions Congress over past governance following Rahul Gandhi jibe
articles.title: Kiren Rijiju hits back at Rahul Gandhi’s 'compromised PM' jibe, questions Congress on 1962 war, poverty
articles.summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday regarding his compromised prime minister remark directed at Narendra Modi. Rijiju challenged the opposition party on social media to apologize for the 1962 Chinese war humiliation and explain India's historical poverty. This exchange followed Gandhi's comments on a trilateral meeting at the APEC summit in China.
articles.description: The Congress leader's remarks triggered a war of words between the BJP and the opposition party, with several BJP leaders accusing Rahul Gandhi of being "clueless" about global geopolitics

articles.headline: Teenager develops severe kidney ailment after using online fairness cream
articles.title: Keralam girl develops kidney ailment after ‘using’ fairness cream promoted on social media
articles.summary: A 17-year-old girl in Keralam developed membranous nephropathy after using a fairness cream ordered online through Instagram promotion, doctors at Aster MIMS Mother Hospital stated on November 21, 2026. Nephrologist Gowri S reported dangerously high mercury levels in the patient's blood and the product. The family plans to initiate legal proceedings against the company in the consumer court.
articles.description: Nephrologist, who is treating the girl, said medical examinations detected dangerously high mercury levels in the 17-year-old’s body. Tests on the cream allegedly found mercury levels of 12,500 parts per million, far exceeding permissible limit of less than 1 ppm, the doctor said

articles.headline: Israeli opposition alliance faces internal strain amid caretaker Prime Minister Netanyahu moves
articles.title: Can Israel’s opposition bloc stay united against Netanyahu?
articles.summary: Israel's opposition change bloc faces internal divisions as caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu attempts to fracture the alliance ahead of the December 6 government formation deadline. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett held a security meeting with Netanyahu, sparking criticism within the 48-seat opposition coalition led by Gadi Eisenkot, which struggles with deep ideological differences.
articles.description: Eisenkot's fragile alliance must overcome deep ideological divisions to turn its opposition into a government.

articles.headline: Mirra Andreeva wins WTA Finals to cap breakthrough tennis season
articles.title: Perfect week caps Mirra Andreeva’s star-making year
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old tennis player Mirra Andreeva won the season-ending Women's Tennis Association Finals in Indian Wells, California, without dropping a single set. She became the youngest champion at the tournament since Maria Sharapova in 2004. Andreeva achieved the victory following a successful year that included a Roland-Garros triumph and a milestone fifty match wins, motivated by a desire to defeat top-ten opponents.
articles.description: The 19-year-old demolished the field at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. The dominant performance against the world’s best, ending a season in which she won her first Major title, suggests she is growing into a player who can ⁠shape the future of women’s tennis

articles.headline: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake strikes central Peru without causing immediate damage
articles.title: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake shakes Peru’s Andes, with no damage or casualties immediately reported
articles.summary: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Andes in central Peru at 7:09 pm local time on Friday, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. The epicentre was located 34 kilometres north of Junin at a depth of 108 kilometres. Peru's Geophysical Institute reported no immediate damage or casualties, though the tremor was felt in the capital.
articles.description: Peru's Geophysical Institute said no damage or casualties had been reported. The earthquake was felt in the Peruvian capital, prompting residents to rush into the streets

articles.headline: Cricket Australia backs Pat Cummins to remain Test captain amid scandal fallout
articles.title: Pat Cummins wins Cricket Australia's ‘unanimous support’ to remain Test captain
articles.summary: Cricket Australia endorsed Pat Cummins as Test captain on November 21, 2026, dismissing integrity concerns following renewed fallout from the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal. Chairman David Boon stated the board rejects any implication against Cummins. The decision follows claims by Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft that the entire team knew of the ball-tampering plot in South Africa. Pacer Josh Hazlewood threatened to quit if Cummins was removed.
articles.description: Cummins has been under huge pressure since Usman Khawaja claimed the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball in a Test at Cape Town in 2018

articles.headline: Funeral held for New York teen shot while walking to school
articles.title: Funeral held for New York teen shot while walking to school
articles.description: Funeral held for New York teen shot while walking to school

articles.headline: IRDAI imposes two crore penalty on Star Health
articles.title: IRDAI imposes ₹2 cr penalty on Star Health
articles.summary: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India levied a two crore penalty on Star Health and Allied Insurance Company following an inspection conducted from January 31 to February 11, 2022. The regulator stated the insurer processed claims inconsistently with policy terms and health insurance regulations regarding Covid claim settlements and arbitrary deductions.
